pathway.title: Sensata Technologies Holding plc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Deleveraging is cash-funded and is the main reason leverage no longer constrains the credit. Carrying-value net debt fell from USD 2,276.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 1,859.6 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 1,877.1 million pro forma for the dividend approved in October 2026, and on adjusted EBITDA net leverage fell from 2.72x to 2.08x, of which debt reduction explains 0.50x and higher earnings 0.14x. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

The sharper fall on reported EBITDA overstates the repair, because the 2025 goodwill impairment left the trailing window: reported net leverage fell 2.18x, of which debt reduction explains 0.82x and the earnings recovery 1.36x, so the adjusted view is the cleaner guide to progress. Basis: calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Free cash flow is the strongest support and is rising. It was 44.52% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2024, 58.66% in FY2025 and 71.89% over the last twelve months, or USD 641.2 million, which would repay carrying-value debt in 3.76 years; part of the 2026 gain is a USD 53.1 million working-capital inflow that could reverse. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

Liquidity and the maturity profile give a long runway before refinancing matters. Cash was USD 553.4 million at 2026-09-30, with pro forma cash for the dividend approved in October 2026 not established, and the revolver was undrawn at USD 645.8 million, so liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million is 5.78x the USD 207.3 million of notes due in April 2029; the revolver matures on 2030-09-24, weeks after notes due 2030-09-01, so 2030 is the pinch point. Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

Refinancing is a cost risk more than an access risk. 91.39% of note principal, USD 2,200.0 million, falls due in 2030 to 2032 against a weighted average coupon of 4.93%, and quarter-end fair values were below principal for every series, from 90.29% to 99.38%, so replacement debt would likely carry a higher coupon; the documents give no yield or spread, so the size of any step-up is not established. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

Earnings are stable on the issuer's adjusted measure but depend on large add-backs and have not been tested by a volume downturn. Adjusted EBITDA margin held between 22.45% and 22.56% from FY2023 to FY2025 and reached 23.18% over the last twelve months, yet add-backs were USD 326.1 million, 63.97% of reported EBITDA, in FY2025 and USD 80.2 million, 9.88%, over the last twelve months, and the FY2025 revenue fall of 5.80% came from divestitures with organic growth of 0.1%. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C18; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

Automotive concentration is the primary downside exposure. Automotive was 57.0% of FY2025 revenue and 53.37% of segment operating income, and the issuer's presentation, citing S&P, expects global light vehicle production to fall 2% in 2026, while Industrials and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment, at 21.3% and 21.7% of revenue, grew faster in the third quarter. Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 100; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 17; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Tariffs have been absorbed by pricing so far, but the exposure is structural. The company passed through USD 40.8 million, 1.10% of FY2025 revenue, about 61% of revenue is earned outside the United States, and the annual report states that raw-material price increases have historically been hard to pass on; refunds after the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling are uncertain and excluded from guidance. Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19

Financial policy turned creditor-friendly in 2026 but is reversible. Cash of USD 431.8 million retired debt in nine months against USD 77.5 million returned to shareholders, yet the borrowing group's distribution capacity is wide and USD 257.3 million of repurchase authorization remains, which Business & governance rates as a medium sponsor and governance risk. Basis: calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14

Book equity gives little asset-based protection. Goodwill and intangibles were 52.73% of total assets at 2026-09-30 and tangible equity was negative USD 459.0 million, so creditor protection rests on going-concern earnings. Basis: calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 2

blocks.title: Company and operating model

cells.text: Sensata Technologies Holding plc, the reporting entity of the consolidated group

Global industrial technology company that develops, manufactures and sells sensors and sensor-rich solutions, electrical protection components and systems, and power conversion products, in three reportable segments: Automotive, Industrials, and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment

United Kingdom: public limited company incorporated in England and Wales, headquartered in Swindon, Wiltshire, with U.S. headquarters in Attleboro, Massachusetts; ordinary shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange
Industrial technology: sensing and electrical protection for automotive, industrial, aerospace, defense and commercial equipment markets
Sensors and high-voltage electrical protection for vehicle makers and their Tier 1 suppliers and aftermarket distributors; USD 2,111.7 million, 57.00% of FY2025 net revenue
Sensors, power management and electrical protection for appliance, HVAC, material handling, energy and charging markets; USD 787.8 million, 21.27% of FY2025 net revenue

rows.label: Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment segment

cells.text: Sensors, electrical protection and operator controls for aircraft, defense, trucks, construction and agriculture; USD 805.0 million, 21.73% of FY2025 net revenue
Vehicle makers, Tier 1 suppliers, industrial manufacturers and integrators; no customer exceeded 10% of net revenue and the top ten customers average 36 years of relationship
Solutions are customized for each application and platform; management states sensors are rarely changed during platform life cycles of five to seven years

About 61% of FY2025 revenue came from subsidiaries outside the United States, about 20% from China; 92% of employees work outside the United States; net property, plant and equipment is largest in China at USD 254.3 million

FY2025 gross margin 29.27%; segment operating margins 23.72% Automotive, 28.69% Industrials and 26.27% Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment, before USD 344.1 million of corporate and other costs
Capital expenditure USD 131.2 million, 3.54% of FY2025 revenue; up to about USD 150.0 million expected in FY2026
Industrials is stronger in the first two quarters; Automotive is weaker in the third quarter
USD 40.8 million of tariffs incurred and passed through to customers in FY2025

blocks.note: Segment operating margins are stated before corporate and other costs, which were USD 344.1 million in FY2025. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 100

runs.text: - Free cash flow and cash-funded deleveraging are the main support. Free cash flow reached USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months while USD 781.8 million of notes were bought from cash between November 2025 and the third quarter of 2026, which cut adjusted net leverage to 2.08x and lowers interest cost and refinancing need. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Liquidity is the second support. Cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 1,199.2 million and no note matures before April 2029, so a downturn would be absorbed before refinancing is needed. Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13

- Customer breadth and design-in positions are the third support. No customer exceeded 10% of revenue, the top ten customers average 36 years of relationship and sensors are rarely changed within five-to-seven-year platforms, which makes revenue visible across a platform cycle even without contracts or a stated backlog. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Adjusted margin stability is the fourth support. Adjusted EBITDA margin stayed at 22.45% to 22.56% through FY2023 to FY2025, so cost actions have so far kept earnings in line with revenue. Basis: calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

- Flexible capital spending and distributions are the fifth support. Capital expenditure fell to 2.34% of revenue and distributions took 13.89% of operating cash flow in nine months of 2026, so both can be cut in a downturn. Basis: calculation C11; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Automotive cyclicality is the main weakness. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income and global light vehicle production is expected to fall in 2026, so a volume decline would reach profit and cash flow first through this segment. Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 100; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18

- Earnings quality is the second weakness. Add-backs were 63.97% of reported EBITDA in FY2025 and USD 100.4 million even after removing the goodwill impairment, so the adjusted figure that makes leverage look moderate depends on recurring restructuring-type charges. Basis: calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

- Tariffs and trade policy are the third weakness. Most revenue is earned outside the United States and the filings state that annual price reductions are demanded by customers and raw-material increases are hard to pass on, so margins are exposed if tariff pass-through stops. Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19

- Concentrated 2030 to 2032 maturities are the fourth weakness. USD 2,200.0 million, 91.39% of note principal, falls due in three years and the revolver expires in 2030, so refinancing cost and timing matter more than access. Basis: calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85

- The acquisition record and wide distribution capacity are the fifth weakness. Dynapower goodwill of USD 375.8 million was written off over 2024 and 2025 and the baskets would allow cash to leave the borrowing group, so financial policy depends on management restraint. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, pages 88–89

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The documents describe no acquisition, merger, sponsor or take-private transaction, pending or completed, in 2025 or 2026, and no new debt issue since the USD 500.0 million of 6.625% notes due 2032 priced at par on 2024-06-06, which with cash redeemed USD 700.0 million of 5.0% notes in July 2024. The revolver is undrawn and its commitments were cut from USD 750.0 million to USD 650.0 million, with maturity extended to 2030-09-24, by the Fourteenth Amendment of 2025-09-24; a technical amendment dated 2026-04-13 conformed its language. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 86; 10-Q_2026-03-31_st.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13

Transactions since late 2025 have been voluntary debt purchases from cash: USD 354.0 million of principal of the 4.0% notes for USD 350.0 million in November 2025, USD 406.1 million for USD 400.0 million in June 2026 and USD 32.6 million for USD 31.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, leaving USD 207.3 million of that series outstanding. Disposals have been modest: the Insights Business went to an affiliate of Balmoral Funds for a purchase price of USD 165.0 million in 2024 and the Magnetic Speed and Position Business closed in the first quarter of 2025. Basis: calculation K11; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-06-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2024-12-31_st.pdf, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102

After the quarter end the board approved a dividend of USD 0.12 per share payable in November 2026 to holders of record on 2026-11-11, about USD 17.5 million on the shares outstanding at 2026-10-14; an executive separation was agreed on 2026-10-22, and Amendment No. 1 to the Domestic Security Agreement is dated 2026-10-26, with its terms not described. No pro forma leverage is stated in the documents for these events. Basis: calculation K16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 44

fields.value: Financial foundation for Sensata Technologies Holding plc as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage on the plc's consolidated figures to the third quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sensata's balance sheet is stronger, with net debt at 2.29x LTM reported EBITDA (2.08x adjusted) against 4.47x at year-end 2025, but most of that improvement comes from the 2025 impairment leaving the earnings window rather than from debt repaid.

Cash of USD 553.4 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 645.8 million sit against a first note maturity of USD 207.3 million in 2029. Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026 interim periods, so interim interest cover is not established; the FY2025 figure is 3.25x.

fields.value: Leverage trajectory. Carrying-value debt fell from USD 2,849.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 2,413.0 million at 2026-09-30 because the issuer spent cash on a June 2026 tender of USD 406.1 million of 4.0% notes for USD 400.0 million and on third-quarter open-market purchases of USD 32.6 million of principal, while cash fell only from USD 573.0 million to USD 553.4 million, so net debt fell by USD 417.2 million to USD 1,859.6 million. Debt reduction explains 0.82x of the 2.18x fall in reported net leverage and the recovery of trailing reported EBITDA from USD 509.8 million to USD 811.7 million explains 1.36x, mostly because the third-quarter 2025 goodwill impairment of USD 225.7 million left the window. Creditors therefore hold real but smaller protection from debt repaid than the headline ratio suggests.

fields.value: Coverage. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 3.25x in FY2025 and 2.98x in FY2024, and adjusted EBITDA covered it 5.32x and 5.97x. Interest expense in the first nine months of 2026 was USD 96.8 million against USD 113.4 million a year earlier, which points to better coverage in 2026, but cash interest paid is not printed for interim periods, so the interim ratio is not established and the improvement rests on expense, not cash.

Operating cash flow was USD 621.5 million in FY2025 and USD 557.8 million in the first nine months of 2026, after USD 131.2 million and USD 68.5 million of capital expenditure, leaving calculated free cash flow of USD 490.3 million and USD 489.3 million. Working capital supplied USD 53.1 million of the 2026 nine-month operating cash flow against an outflow of USD 23.6 million a year earlier, so part of the 2026 cash flow could reverse if receivables and inventory rebuild.

fields.value: Liquidity. Cash of USD 553.4 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 645.8 million, together USD 1,199.2 million or 0.50x total debt, face a debt profile with no maturity before 2029 and a first maturity of USD 207.3 million. Shareholder returns are the main discretionary use: USD 52.4 million of dividends and USD 25.1 million of buybacks in nine months, and the October 2026 dividend would add about USD 17.5 million to net debt.

fields.value: Data quality and definitions. Reported EBITDA of USD 509.8 million for FY2025 is struck after USD 307.0 million of restructuring-related and other add-backs that include a non-cash goodwill impairment, and the issuer restated its adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 from USD 881.6 million to USD 882.8 million, so adjusted series are comparable only on the later definition. Several printed totals differ from their components by 0.1 through rounding; where the filing itself prints the difference, the total is left unsupplied and logged under the gap lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contrary evidence. The issuer-adjusted view of 2.08x net and strong free cash flow argue that leverage was already moderate before the repayments, and that view wins if add-backs fall as they did from USD 326.1 million in FY2025 to USD 80.2 million over the last twelve months and if working capital inflows persist. Monitoring should watch interim cash interest, any new restructuring add-backs and working capital in the next report.

fields.value: | Board and control rights | Twelve directors are listed; the Chief Executive Officer is the only executive among them and the Chairman is a separate director; the committees are Audit, Compensation, Nominating and Corporate Governance, Finance, and Innovation and Technology, and the Audit Committee has four members | Supportive | A separate chair and an audit committee without executives give independent oversight of reporting and financing decisions, and no controlling holder is named | Lowers the chance that one holder directs distributions or financing against creditors, but does not bind the board | High | 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 117 | Director independence is not stated and the proxy statement was not supplied |

fields.value: | Shareholder rights and statutory limits | Dividends, distributions and repurchases may be paid only out of distributable reserves; shareholders approve the form of repurchase contracts and the directors' authority to allot shares, with approval renewed at each annual meeting; off-market purchases need shareholder approval for up to five years | Supportive | English company law caps value leaving the parent at its realized reserves and sends repurchase terms to shareholders, a limit that sits beside the covenant baskets | Adds a statutory ceiling on distributions that does not depend on lender consent | High | 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 30 | The amount of distributable reserves is not stated in the documents supplied |

fields.value: | Audit status and reporting quality | Deloitte & Touche LLP gave an unqualified opinion on the 2025 statements and found internal control effective at 2025-12-31; management completed remediation of material weaknesses disclosed in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports and the quarterly reports through September 2025, affecting inventory and account reconciliation processes in shared services in Mexico, and a new Chief Accounting Officer joined in May 2024; the 2024 audit report carried an adverse opinion on internal control | Mixed | Weak controls over inventory and reconciliations raise the risk of misstated earnings and working capital, the inputs to leverage and liquidity tests; the 2025 opinion shows the repair but only one clean year exists | Restores reliance on reported EBITDA and cash, but durability is unproven until a second clean year | High | 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, pages 105–107; 10-K_2024-12-31_st.pdf, page 66 | The 2023 annual report was not supplied, so the 2023 weaknesses are known only from the 2025 description |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | Covenant reporting and certificates | Management states compliance with all covenants and default provisions at 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30; the only financial maintenance covenant is a senior secured net leverage ratio not above 5.0x, tested when loans and uncollateralized letters of credit exceed 30% of revolver commitments; compliance certificates were not supplied | Neutral | While the revolver is undrawn apart from USD 4.2 million of letters of credit, the maintenance test does not apply, so covenant reporting gives creditors little early signal | Monitoring rests on the incurrence limits and on reported results rather than on a headroom test | High | 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 88; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 40 | Covenant EBITDA definition and any compliance certificate were not supplied |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for Sensata Technologies Holding plc as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: the business, transaction history, ownership, governance, shareholder behavior and capital allocation, from the eleven supplied documents and the source readiness findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sensata is a widely held public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so creditors face moderate governance risk from shareholder returns and past acquisition write-offs rather than from sponsor extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 management put debt reduction ahead of shareholder returns, retiring debt with USD 431.8 million of cash in nine months against USD 77.5 million returned to shareholders, and the internal control weaknesses disclosed in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports were remediated by year-end 2025. Risk stays moderate because the credit agreement permits large distributions, the executed documents were not supplied, and USD 375.8 million of Dynapower goodwill was written off in 2024 and 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K10; calculation K12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, pages 105–107; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, pages 88–89

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes the sponsor-extraction mechanism but leaves public shareholders as the force behind distributions. Three holders of record, one of them the depository nominee, held the ordinary shares at 2026-01-29, and the proxy statement that would show beneficial holders, related-party dealings and pay incentives was not supplied, so the finding rests on the absence of any sponsor in the filings and not on a holder list.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns have been subordinated to debt reduction since mid-2025 but remain a lever that can be pulled back. Dividends and repurchases took 41.31% of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2025 and 30.73% in FY2025, against 13.89% in the first nine months of 2026, and repurchases fell to USD 25.1 million from USD 120.6 million a year earlier; USD 257.3 million of authorization remains with no expiry date, so a change of priority would not need lender consent within the distribution baskets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liability management has so far favored creditors. Three voluntary purchases between November 2025 and the third quarter of 2026 retired USD 792.7 million of 4.0% note principal for USD 781.8 million of cash, with the revolver undrawn, and the documents describe no exchange, uptier, priming or drop-down; the company does reserve the right to retire or exchange debt in other ways, in amounts that may be material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K11; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-06-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legal capacity to move cash out of the borrowing group is wide, but no use beyond ordinary dividends and repurchases is documented, so capacity is a risk and not yet a behavior. As summarized in the annual report, distributions to the parent companies may reach USD 50.0 million a year plus unlimited amounts while senior secured net leverage is at or below 2.5x, 7.0% of market capitalization a year, and the greater of USD 150.0 million and 20.0% of covenant EBITDA, and the credit agreement lets unrestricted subsidiaries be designated, although none has been; these terms rest on the issuer's summary because the executed documents were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting quality has been repaired, but the clean record is one year long. Material weaknesses in internal control, disclosed in the 2023 and 2024 annual reports and in quarterly reports through September 2025 and centered on inventory and account reconciliation processes in shared services in Mexico, were declared remediated at 2025-12-31, and the auditor's opinion on internal control was adverse for 2024 and unqualified for 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition record is the main governance concern. Dynapower goodwill of USD 375.8 million was impaired in the third quarters of 2024 and 2025 with USD 4.1 million left, and the Insights Business, impaired by USD 321.7 million in 2023, was sold in 2024 for a purchase price of USD 165.0 million against net assets of about USD 263.4 million; the write-offs are non-cash, but they show that acquisition capital earned less than its cost while management still names acquisitions as an option.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 96; 10-K_2024-12-31_st.pdf, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified across three segments with low single-customer concentration, yet it stays tied to the automotive cycle. Automotive was 57.0% of FY2025 revenue, Industrials 21.3% and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment 21.7%, no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, and the top ten customers have averaged 36 years of relationship; in the third quarter of 2026 Industrials and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment grew 12.6% and 13.4% against 3.7% for Automotive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K1; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating momentum supports debt service, but the third quarter was flattered by a one-time payment. Revenue grew 5.11% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and segment operating income rose to USD 770.0 million from USD 680.3 million; the third quarter included USD 24.0 million from a customer for a cancelled electric vehicle program, so its growth was 7.68% reported and 5.11% without it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K5; calculation K6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operations are weighted outside the United States, which adds tariff and trade-policy exposure. Subsidiaries outside the United States earned about 61% of FY2025 revenue, about 20% of it in China, and 92% of employees work outside the United States; the company incurred and passed through USD 40.8 million of tariffs in FY2025, and potential refunds after the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling are uncertain and excluded from fourth-quarter guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K7; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Guarantee coverage is thinner than the group's size suggests: the non-U.S. subsidiaries of the borrower were released as guarantors in August 2023, with a conditional duty to reinstate that the documents do not describe, while subsidiaries outside the United States generated about 61% of FY2025 revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a lower risk level is that management reports deleveraging ahead of schedule, ratings are stable at BB+ from S&P and Ba2 from Moody's, internal control now tests as effective, and nothing in the record shows value moving to shareholders at creditors' expense; the level would fall to Low if the executed documents show distribution baskets that tighten as leverage rises and a second clean year-end controls result follows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a higher level is that capacity is wide, shareholders received USD 173.5 million in the first nine months of 2025 before the change of priority, USD 257.3 million of repurchase authorization is unused, and Dynapower shows that acquisitions have lost money; the level would rise to High on a debt-funded acquisition, a return to heavy repurchases while leverage is elevated, the designation of an unrestricted subsidiary, any further guarantee release or non-pro-rata exchange, or a new material weakness in internal control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 88

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so beneficial holders, board independence, related-party dealings and pay incentives are not established; the finding that no controlling shareholder exists would change if a large holder appears in it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement, indentures and amendments were not supplied, so every statement about distribution, guarantee and unrestricted-subsidiary capacity rests on the issuer's own summary and could change when the baskets, definitions and the 2025 and 2026 amendments are read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The purchase price and funding of the Dynapower acquisition are not stated, so the acquisition finding rests on write-offs alone and cannot say whether the original deal was debt funded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No lender compliance certificate or basket-usage report was supplied, so the statement that covenants were met is management's, and the distribution-capacity finding cannot be tied to headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment figures are on different bases in the 2025 annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports, after products moved between segments, so a shift in business mix between FY2025 and 2026 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management's statement that deleveraging is its top capital allocation priority is an intention and not a commitment, so the moderate risk level would rise if returns to shareholders went back to their 2025 pace.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Segment operating margins are stated before corporate and other costs, which were USD 344.1 million in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Market capitalization and enterprise value are the issuer's own figures at 2026-09-30, and holder detail is limited to the record holders the annual report states.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The documents describe no acquisition, merger, sponsor or take-private transaction, pending or completed, in 2025 or 2026, and no new debt issue since the USD 500.0 million of 6.625% notes due 2032 priced at par on 2024-06-06, which with cash redeemed USD 700.0 million of 5.0% notes in July 2024. The revolver is undrawn and its commitments were cut from USD 750.0 million to USD 650.0 million, with maturity extended to 2030-09-24, by the Fourteenth Amendment of 2025-09-24; a technical amendment dated 2026-04-13 conformed its language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Transactions since late 2025 have been voluntary debt purchases from cash: USD 354.0 million of principal of the 4.0% notes for USD 350.0 million in November 2025, USD 406.1 million for USD 400.0 million in June 2026 and USD 32.6 million for USD 31.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, leaving USD 207.3 million of that series outstanding. Disposals have been modest: the Insights Business went to an affiliate of Balmoral Funds for a purchase price of USD 165.0 million in 2024 and the Magnetic Speed and Position Business closed in the first quarter of 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K11; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-06-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2024-12-31_st.pdf, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After the quarter end the board approved a dividend of USD 0.12 per share payable in November 2026 to holders of record on 2026-11-11, about USD 17.5 million on the shares outstanding at 2026-10-14; an executive separation was agreed on 2026-10-22, and Amendment No. 1 to the Domestic Security Agreement is dated 2026-10-26, with its terms not described. No pro forma leverage is stated in the documents for these events.

fields.value: Module status: ready with limitations, because the proxy statement and the executed financing documents were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. The level is driven by shareholder-return policy and the acquisition record, because they move cash and capital away from creditors, which implies moderate leakage and acquisition risk; the countervailing evidence is the debt reduction since 2025 and the remediated controls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 1 | Automotive volume and price exposure | Automotive was 57.0% of FY2025 revenue and 53.37% of segment operating income; the issuer cites an S&P forecast of a 2% fall in 2026 light vehicle production | Lower volumes reduce absorption of fixed manufacturing costs and annual customer price cuts compound the margin effect | Raises default-probability sensitivity to the automotive cycle and is the primary downside path | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 2 | Cash-funded deleveraging | Net debt fell from USD 2,276.8 million to USD 1,859.6 million; reported net leverage 4.47x to 2.29x (2.31x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend); adjusted 2.72x to 2.08x | Lower debt cuts interest expense and the refinancing amount ahead of 2029 to 2032 | Reduces leverage tolerance risk and improves refinancing capacity | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 3 | Free cash flow generation | Last-twelve-month free cash flow USD 641.2 million, 71.89% of adjusted EBITDA against 44.52% in FY2024; debt would be repaid in 3.76 years of that cash flow | Capital spending below depreciation and a working-capital inflow lift conversion, but operating cash flow also rose | Supports debt service and further retirement of notes; part of the gain may reverse | Positive | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 4 | Liquidity and near-term maturities | Cash USD 553.4 million plus undrawn revolver USD 645.8 million is USD 1,199.2 million, 5.78x the USD 207.3 million due in April 2029 | No maturity for about 29 months and an undrawn committed facility remove near-term refinancing pressure | Limits liquidity-distress risk within the horizon | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 5 | Earnings quality and add-backs | Add-backs USD 326.1 million, 63.97% of reported EBITDA in FY2025 and USD 80.2 million, 9.88%, over the last twelve months; USD 100.4 million excluding the goodwill impairment | Recurring restructuring-type charges mean adjusted EBITDA overstates cash earnings available to creditors | Leverage on reported EBITDA is the more cautious guide; adjusted leverage carries more judgement | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 6 | Tariff and trade exposure | USD 40.8 million of tariffs passed through in FY2025, 1.10% of revenue; about 61% of revenue earned outside the United States; refunds uncertain | Loss of pass-through or new tariffs would compress margin, and customer price demands limit recovery | Adds margin and cash-flow volatility | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 7 | 2030 to 2032 refinancing concentration | USD 2,200.0 million, 91.39% of notes, due 2030 to 2032; weighted average coupon 4.93%; fair values 90.29% to 99.38% of principal; revolver matures 2030-09-24 | Refinancing at market yields above low coupons would raise interest cost, and the 2030 notes and revolver fall due together | Cost and timing risk rather than access risk; early action would reduce it | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 8 | Shareholder returns and acquisition record | Returns took 41.31% of operating cash flow in nine months of 2025 and 13.89% in 2026; USD 257.3 million authorization remains; Dynapower goodwill of USD 375.8 million written off | Wide distribution capacity and a weak acquisition record let value leave or be lost if priorities change | Financial policy is the swing factor for leverage; assessed as medium governance risk | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 9 | Customer breadth and design-in positions | No customer above 10% of revenue; top ten customers average 36 years of relationship; sensors rarely changed within five-to-seven-year platforms; Industrials and the third segment grew 12.6% and 13.4% in the third quarter | Broad customers limit single-name loss and design-in cuts switching, though contracts and backlog are not stated | Supports revenue visibility and stable earnings in a flat market | Positive | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 10 | Adjusted margin stability | Adjusted EBITDA margin FY2023 22.50%, FY2024 22.45%, FY2025 22.56% and 23.18% over the last twelve months | Cost actions kept margin steady while revenue fell from divestitures, but no organic volume decline tests it | Supports earnings durability with the test still to come | Positive | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 11 | Thin asset base | Goodwill and intangibles 52.73% of total assets; tangible equity negative USD 459.0 million | Book assets offer little protection if earnings fall | Creditor protection rests on going-concern earnings | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | Revenue decline | Fourth-quarter 2026 revenue below the guided USD 942 million to USD 972 million, or negative organic growth in Automotive | Revenue is the first line to show a volume downturn in a segment that earns most segment profit | Lower revenue would pressure margin and free cash flow and raise leverage | PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 17 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | EBITDA margin pressure | Adjusted operating margin below the guided 19.6% to 19.8% in the fourth quarter, or adjusted EBITDA margin below the 22.45% to 22.56% range of FY2023 to FY2025 | Margin is the buffer between a revenue fall and cash flow | A lower margin cuts free cash flow and slows deleveraging | PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1) |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | FCF deterioration | Free cash flow conversion below the level above 100% of adjusted net income that management targets for 2026, or a reversal of the USD 53.1 million working-capital inflow | Conversion is the main source of debt retirement | Lower cash generation would stall retirement of notes | PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | Liquidity reduction | Revolver loans plus uncollateralized letters of credit above USD 195.0 million, 30% of USD 650.0 million of commitments, which activates the 5.0x senior secured net leverage test; or cash falling well below USD 553.4 million | A draw signals cash stress and brings a maintenance covenant into force | Would cut liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million and raise default risk | 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; Headroom under the test is not calculated here |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | Leverage increase | Reported net leverage rising above 2.29x at 2026-09-30 (2.31x pro forma for the October 2026 dividend); issuer-reported net leverage above 2.1x | Leverage is the headline measure of progress | A rise would reverse deleveraging and weaken refinancing capacity | Financial foundation (CP-1); PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 15 |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | Refinancing delay | No refinancing or cash retirement of the 2030 notes and revolver as the April 2029 maturity approaches; fair values of the 2031 notes staying near 90.29% of principal | The 2030 notes and the revolver expiry fall together | Delay would raise refinancing cost and timing risk | 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; Quantitative threshold not available in provided materials |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | Sponsor/shareholder action | Share repurchases resuming at the 2025 pace of USD 120.6 million in nine months, a debt-funded acquisition, an unrestricted subsidiary designation, or a further guarantee release | These actions would move cash or assets away from creditors | Would raise leakage and acquisition risk and lift the governance risk level | 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 88; Business & governance (CP-1A) |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Sensata Technologies Holding plc as of 2026-11-18. Pathway: credit snapshot. Scope: the overall fundamental credit profile, its strongest support, weakest dimension and primary downside, built on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance findings and the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sensata's fundamental credit profile is adequate and improving, as cash-funded debt retirement and rising free cash flow have cut leverage sharply, but automotive cyclicality, tariff exposure and add-back-heavy earnings leave creditors exposed to a volume downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported net leverage fell from 4.47x at 2025-12-31 to 2.29x at 2026-09-30, or 2.31x pro forma for the quarterly dividend approved in October 2026, and liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million covers the first maturity, in April 2029, 5.78x. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income and 91.39% of note principal falls due in 2030 to 2032, so the profile is adequate and not strong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging is cash-funded and is the main reason leverage no longer constrains the credit. Carrying-value net debt fell from USD 2,276.8 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 1,859.6 million at 2026-09-30, or USD 1,877.1 million pro forma for the dividend approved in October 2026, and on adjusted EBITDA net leverage fell from 2.72x to 2.08x, of which debt reduction explains 0.50x and higher earnings 0.14x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sharper fall on reported EBITDA overstates the repair, because the 2025 goodwill impairment left the trailing window: reported net leverage fell 2.18x, of which debt reduction explains 0.82x and the earnings recovery 1.36x, so the adjusted view is the cleaner guide to progress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is the strongest support and is rising. It was 44.52% of adjusted EBITDA in FY2024, 58.66% in FY2025 and 71.89% over the last twelve months, or USD 641.2 million, which would repay carrying-value debt in 3.76 years; part of the 2026 gain is a USD 53.1 million working-capital inflow that could reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity profile give a long runway before refinancing matters. Cash was USD 553.4 million at 2026-09-30, with pro forma cash for the dividend approved in October 2026 not established, and the revolver was undrawn at USD 645.8 million, so liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million is 5.78x the USD 207.3 million of notes due in April 2029; the revolver matures on 2030-09-24, weeks after notes due 2030-09-01, so 2030 is the pinch point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing is a cost risk more than an access risk. 91.39% of note principal, USD 2,200.0 million, falls due in 2030 to 2032 against a weighted average coupon of 4.93%, and quarter-end fair values were below principal for every series, from 90.29% to 99.38%, so replacement debt would likely carry a higher coupon; the documents give no yield or spread, so the size of any step-up is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are stable on the issuer's adjusted measure but depend on large add-backs and have not been tested by a volume downturn. Adjusted EBITDA margin held between 22.45% and 22.56% from FY2023 to FY2025 and reached 23.18% over the last twelve months, yet add-backs were USD 326.1 million, 63.97% of reported EBITDA, in FY2025 and USD 80.2 million, 9.88%, over the last twelve months, and the FY2025 revenue fall of 5.80% came from divestitures with organic growth of 0.1%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C18; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Automotive concentration is the primary downside exposure. Automotive was 57.0% of FY2025 revenue and 53.37% of segment operating income, and the issuer's presentation, citing S&P, expects global light vehicle production to fall 2% in 2026, while Industrials and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment, at 21.3% and 21.7% of revenue, grew faster in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 100; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 17; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariffs have been absorbed by pricing so far, but the exposure is structural. The company passed through USD 40.8 million, 1.10% of FY2025 revenue, about 61% of revenue is earned outside the United States, and the annual report states that raw-material price increases have historically been hard to pass on; refunds after the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling are uncertain and excluded from guidance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy turned creditor-friendly in 2026 but is reversible. Cash of USD 431.8 million retired debt in nine months against USD 77.5 million returned to shareholders, yet the borrowing group's distribution capacity is wide and USD 257.3 million of repurchase authorization remains, which Business & governance rates as a medium sponsor and governance risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Book equity gives little asset-based protection. Goodwill and intangibles were 52.73% of total assets at 2026-09-30 and tangible equity was negative USD 459.0 million, so creditor protection rests on going-concern earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that adjusted net leverage of 2.08x is already moderate, free cash flow of USD 641.2 million would repay carrying-value debt in 3.76 years, interest expense of USD 132.5 million over the last twelve months is covered 6.73x by adjusted EBITDA, ratings are stable at BB+ from S&P and Ba2 from Moody's, and the issuer cites an equity value of USD 6.0 billion; the profile would move to strong after a period of lower volumes in which margins and free cash flow hold, with add-backs staying below 10% of reported EBITDA and the 2030 notes refinanced early.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 40; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a worse view is that no volume downturn sits in the record, capital expenditure of 2.34% of revenue in nine months is 67.09% of depreciation after 4.55% in FY2023, the working-capital inflow can reverse, and shareholder returns reached USD 173.5 million in the first nine months of 2025; the profile would move to weak on a sharp fall in automotive volumes with margins falling, a revolver draw above the level that triggers the leverage test, a return to heavy repurchases, a debt-funded acquisition, or a failure to address the 2030 maturities well before they fall due.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 14; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid is not printed for interim periods, so coverage is judged on interest expense for the last twelve months; the adequate view would weaken if cash interest is materially above expense.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2023 to 2025 record contains no organic volume decline, so margin and cash resilience under a downturn are inferred from adjusted margins and documented cost actions and not observed; the margin finding would change after the first volume decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer data or sector benchmark was supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is a judgement from the filings alone and the adequate label has no benchmark.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Note prices are quarter-end estimates from the filings and no yield or spread was supplied, so the size of the refinancing cost step-up is not established and the refinancing finding could move either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No forward credit model was run, so the outlook rests on one quarter of management guidance and the issuer's own full-year targets; the improving trend is not projected beyond them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement and executed financing documents were not supplied, so distribution capacity, guarantee coverage and ranking enter this view only as the issuer's own summary and cannot be tested here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow and cash-funded deleveraging are the main support. Free cash flow reached USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months while USD 781.8 million of notes were bought from cash between November 2025 and the third quarter of 2026, which cut adjusted net leverage to 2.08x and lowers interest cost and refinancing need.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is the second support. Cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 1,199.2 million and no note matures before April 2029, so a downturn would be absorbed before refinancing is needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer breadth and design-in positions are the third support. No customer exceeded 10% of revenue, the top ten customers average 36 years of relationship and sensors are rarely changed within five-to-seven-year platforms, which makes revenue visible across a platform cycle even without contracts or a stated backlog.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Adjusted margin stability is the fourth support. Adjusted EBITDA margin stayed at 22.45% to 22.56% through FY2023 to FY2025, so cost actions have so far kept earnings in line with revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Flexible capital spending and distributions are the fifth support. Capital expenditure fell to 2.34% of revenue and distributions took 13.89% of operating cash flow in nine months of 2026, so both can be cut in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Automotive cyclicality is the main weakness. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income and global light vehicle production is expected to fall in 2026, so a volume decline would reach profit and cash flow first through this segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 100; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings quality is the second weakness. Add-backs were 63.97% of reported EBITDA in FY2025 and USD 100.4 million even after removing the goodwill impairment, so the adjusted figure that makes leverage look moderate depends on recurring restructuring-type charges.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Tariffs and trade policy are the third weakness. Most revenue is earned outside the United States and the filings state that annual price reductions are demanded by customers and raw-material increases are hard to pass on, so margins are exposed if tariff pass-through stops.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Concentrated 2030 to 2032 maturities are the fourth weakness. USD 2,200.0 million, 91.39% of note principal, falls due in three years and the revolver expires in 2030, so refinancing cost and timing matter more than access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The acquisition record and wide distribution capacity are the fifth weakness. Dynapower goodwill of USD 375.8 million was written off over 2024 and 2025 and the baskets would allow cash to leave the borrowing group, so financial policy depends on management restraint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sensata develops, manufactures and sells sensors, electrical protection and power conversion products in three segments, Automotive, Industrials, and Aerospace, Defense, and Commercial Equipment, which were 57.0%, 21.3% and 21.7% of FY2025 revenue. No customer exceeded 10% of revenue and the top ten customers average 36 years of relationship, which supports cash-flow visibility across platform cycles of five to seven years, but the filings state no order backlog and no contracted volumes, so visibility ends at the platform level and automotive and commercial equipment demand remain cyclical. About 61% of revenue is earned by subsidiaries outside the United States, which adds tariff and currency exposure to debt service. The portfolio has been pruned through the 2024 Insights Business sale, the 2025 sale of the Magnetic Speed and Position Business and the exit from Spear, which cut revenue by 6.5% in FY2025 and left a smaller, more focused earnings base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sensata is a widely held English public company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified, so the sponsor-extraction mechanism is absent but beneficial holdings were not supplied. The plc has no debt of its own: the notes are issued by Sensata Technologies B.V. and Sensata Technologies, Inc., both indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries, and the borrower's distributions to its parents are limited by baskets in the credit agreement. Guarantee coverage is thinner since the August 2023 release of non-U.S. guarantors, and the sponsor and governance risk level is medium because of the acquisition record, wide distribution capacity and a one-year clean internal control record; the executed documents were not supplied, so these terms are the issuer's own summary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue follows light vehicle production in Automotive, housing, energy and data center demand in Industrials, and aerospace, truck and construction cycles in the third segment. Pricing power is limited: the annual report states that customers demand annual price reductions and that raw-material increases have historically been hard to pass on, although the USD 40.8 million of FY2025 tariffs was passed through and design-in positions give some protection. Third-quarter revenue growth was 3.7% in Automotive, 12.6% in Industrials and 13.4% in the third segment, with a USD 24.0 million one-time payment for a cancelled electric vehicle program inside Automotive, so revenue is recurring through platform life but exposed to program cancellations and volume swings, and the credit implication is that earnings can be stable in a flat market and uncertain in a falling one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of revenue was 70.73% of FY2025 revenue and consists mainly of production materials and employee costs, with research and development at 3.61% and selling, general and administrative expense at 9.62%. Manufacturing sits in lower-cost countries, notably China, Mexico, Malaysia and Bulgaria, which helps margins but ties them to tariffs and currency. Adjusted EBITDA margin held at 22.45% to 22.56% in FY2023 to FY2025, and gross margin was 31.41% in nine months of 2026 against 29.27% in FY2025, but the record holds no organic volume decline, restructuring charges recurred every year, and metals hedges are not accounting hedges, so margin defence under a volume shock rests on cost actions and pass-through that have not been tested at scale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C17; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure fell from 4.55% of revenue in FY2023 to 3.54% in FY2025 and 2.34% in nine months of 2026, which is 74.46% and 67.09% of depreciation, so part of the cash conversion comes from spending below the asset base's wear, and management expects up to about USD 150.0 million in FY2026. Free cash flow reached USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months, 71.89% of adjusted EBITDA, with cash interest of USD 157.0 million in FY2025 and a nine-month working-capital inflow of USD 53.1 million that may reverse. Capex flexibility and the option to stop repurchases give room to protect cash over the 2029 to 2032 maturity wall, but the conversion gain is part structural and part timing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate in Automotive, where the company competes with three to four suppliers per application, and sharper in Industrials, where low-cost suppliers in China have entered, which caps pricing and margin. New entrants face high switching costs because customers invest in selecting and testing sensors, but competitors influenced by large vehicle makers limit access to some customers. Substitution risk comes from customers producing in-house and from the shift to electrified platforms, which the electrical protection portfolio partly offsets. Buyers hold the stronger hand through annual price reductions, and suppliers of semiconductors, resins and metals can pass on cost swings that the company has found hard to recover, so the forces most relevant to credit are buyer pricing and input costs acting on margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These factors are material to credit and are therefore assessed. Trade policy matters most: tariffs of USD 40.8 million were passed through in FY2025, most Mexican facilities operate under the Maquiladora program whose changes could raise costs, and the February 2026 ruling against certain tariffs leaves potential refunds uncertain and outside guidance. Economic cycles matter through light vehicle production, expected to fall 2% in 2026 on the issuer's cited S&P forecast, and soft U.S. housing in Industrials. Technology cuts both ways: electrification adds high-voltage content, yet slower electric vehicle adoption or cancelled programs, as in the third quarter of 2026, would reduce demand, while data center products, USD 27 million of revenue in 2025 and USD 48 million estimated for 2026, add a small diversifier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 102; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 11; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are cash-funded deleveraging, free cash flow of USD 641.2 million over the last twelve months, liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million with no maturity before 2029, and customer breadth with no customer above 10% of revenue. Weaknesses are the 53.37% share of segment operating income earned in Automotive, add-backs that were 63.97% of reported EBITDA in FY2025, recurring restructuring and goodwill write-offs, and negative tangible equity. Opportunities that could lift credit quality are growth in data center, aerospace and commercial equipment products, further cash retirement of notes, and an early refinancing of the 2030 notes. Threats are a fall in light vehicle production, loss of tariff pass-through, a return to heavy repurchases or debt-funded acquisitions, and a new internal control weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale is strong, with USD 3,704.5 million of revenue in FY2025 and operations in many countries, and business diversification is average because three segments and a broad customer base spread the business but Automotive still dominates profit. Competitive advantage is average: switching costs protect incumbent positions while customers demand price reductions and low-cost rivals have entered Industrials. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with spending and distributions that can be cut but restructuring that has recurred every year. Margin stability is average because adjusted margins are steady but untested by a volume decline, and free cash flow stability is average because conversion is rising yet helped by capital spending below depreciation and a working-capital inflow. Ability to refinance is average, with BB+ and Ba2 ratings and no maturity before 2029 but 91.39% of notes due in 2030 to 2032 and quarter-end prices below par. Liquidity is strong, and financial policy and governance is average because 2026 behavior favors creditors while capacity for distributions is wide. The trend is improving; the datapoints missing for a firmer view are interim cash interest, a volume downturn, peer benchmarks and the executed financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months tailwinds are lower interest, with adjusted net interest expense expected by the issuer at about USD 111 million in 2026 against USD 139 million before its transformation, growth in aerospace, truck and data center markets, and fourth-quarter guidance of USD 942 million to USD 972 million of revenue, 3% to 6% growth, with adjusted operating margin of 19.6% to 19.8%. Headwinds are a 2% fall in 2026 light vehicle production with 4% expected in the fourth quarter, China softness, uncertain tariff refunds, a possible working-capital reversal and capital expenditure of up to about USD 150.0 million in FY2026. Over three to five years the outlook depends on electrified platform adoption, data center and unmanned aircraft ramps from 2027 and 2028, and the 2029 to 2032 refinancing, where lower leverage helps but market pricing is unknown; no forward model was run, so these items are directional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 5; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 8; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 11; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a fall in global light vehicle production beyond the 2% the issuer cites, joined by further electric vehicle program cancellations such as the one that produced a USD 24.0 million payment in the third quarter of 2026. The first operational break is lower Automotive volume, where fixed manufacturing costs are absorbed less and customers keep demanding annual price cuts, so margin falls before revenue restructuring cuts costs. Automotive earned 53.37% of FY2025 segment operating income, so the effect reaches free cash flow quickly, while working capital may reverse the 2026 inflow and tariff refunds are not counted. Liquidity of USD 1,199.2 million, the option to stop repurchases and cut capital expenditure, and no maturity before April 2029 mean the scenario is a leverage and refinancing-cost problem, not a liquidity distress, unless loans and uncollateralized letters of credit on the revolver exceed USD 195.0 million, which would activate the leverage test, or distributions resume. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter revenue below guidance, light vehicle forecast cuts, revolver draws, repurchases and the 2030 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C12; calculation C16; calculation C17; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 18; PRESENTATION_Q32026_st.pdf, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_st.pdf, page 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_st.htm.jsonl, page 20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Sensata presents an adequate business profile supported by customer breadth, design-in positions and stable adjusted margins, but credit quality is constrained by automotive cyclicality, trade exposure and earnings that rely on large add-backs. Cash-flow durability appears adequate to strong because free cash flow is rising and capital spending and distributions are flexible. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2030 cluster of notes and revolver, on how note prices move, and on whether management keeps cash-funded deleveraging ahead of shareholder returns. The primary downside path is a fall in automotive volumes that cuts margin and free cash flow while tariff pass-through weakens and distributions resume. Further analysis would require interim cash interest, executed financing documents, peer benchmarks, market yields and a forward model. Top risk: automotive volume and price pressure on a profit base concentrated in one segment.
